summary: Fourteen days of high-quality CGM data show strong overall time in range but clinically important recurrent hypoglycemia, especially from late evening through early night and after treatment of daytime highs. Daytime hyperglycemia often prompted UAM, SMB, temporary basal, and Dynamic ISF responses with substantial IOB, so it does not independently establish weak basal, CR, or static ISF settings. The safest primary profile candidate is a higher 00:00 target while holding dependent insulin-delivery settings unchanged for observation.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM and device telemetry are adequate for broad temporal analysis. The authoritative profile is complete and was declared historically applicable. Meal-specific analysis remains limited because no carbohydrate treatments or numeric meal-strategy declarations are present.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were 3,995 valid glucose entries, 98.7% coverage, an estimated five-minute cadence, no duplicates, 10 gaps, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. The profile contains complete basal, CR, ISF, target, DIA, and AAPS settings, and profile_context reports historical_applicability as yes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Hourly conclusions use local-time glucose. Basal, correction, and meal interpretations depend on separating loop insulin, IOB, temporary targets, meals, activity, and pump events.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There are no recorded carbohydrate treatments, meal timing details, activity records, hypo-treatment records, or complete event-by-event reconstructions of all insulin preceding each low.

analysis_steps.findings: Recurrent hypoglycemia is the principal safety constraint. High-to-low transitions after daytime hyperglycemia are more important than the favorable average glucose and overall time in range.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose was 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0%, time above range 8.9%, time below range 5.1%, and CV 32.6%. Repeated readings reached 41-42 mg/dL. Local TBR was 10.1-18.5% from 23:00 through 03:00 and 15.3% at 19:00. Daily TBR reached 12.8%.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Any effort to address daytime highs must first account for residual IOB, Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, correction insulin, targets, and late hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Finger-stick confirmation, symptoms, rescue carbohydrates, activity, compression-low annotations, and a separate percentage below 54 mg/dL are unavailable.

analysis_steps.findings: The clearest profile-related concern is the 90 mg/dL target during a recurrent overnight low window. No basal segment has a clean fasting test, and daytime highs do not establish insufficient basal because meal and automation effects remain plausible.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local TBR was 11.4% at 00:00, 18.5% at 01:00, approximately 10% at 02:00-03:00, and 10.1% at 23:00. The 00:00 target is 90 mg/dL. Afternoon TAR reached 22.6-32.1%, but it was followed by increased automated insulin, substantial IOB, and evening lows.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Target interpretation depends on preceding correction and automation IOB. Basal interpretation depends on fasting-like observations without meals, corrections, temporary targets, or activity effects.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No labeled fasting windows or complete preceding-insulin timelines are available.

analysis_steps.findings: No CR segment can be tested from the available meal data. The flat profile ISF cannot be evaluated independently of Dynamic ISF and automated insulin. Glucose effects frequently continued for four to six hours, but the observations neither validate nor refute the 10-hour DIA.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were zero carbohydrate entries. Profile ISF is 56 mg/dL/U, while representative variable sensitivity ranged from approximately 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U. Correction-response windows included large declines and rebounds through six hours, but they were not isolated correction tests.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR depends on meal amount, timing, immediate bolus delivery, and absorption. ISF and DIA depend on complete SMB, temporary basal, correction, IOB, food, activity, and rescue-carbohydrate histories.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There are no isolated meal or correction tests and no response observations beyond six hours for direct assessment of the 10-hour DIA.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are coherently configured, but UAM is carrying most meal-like interpretation because COB is repeatedly zero. Automation may amplify insulin accumulation during rapid rises, although the data cannot isolate SMB/UAM from Dynamic ISF, corrections, or temporary basal.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM are enabled, SMB is always enabled, and the configured ordinary and UAM limits are 15 and 20 basal minutes. Representative episodes showed IOB of 4.73 U and 5.935 U during treatment of highs. Later low patterns occurred in the broader telemetry.
analysis_steps.dependencies: SMB/UAM effects depend on Dynamic ISF, profile ISF, DIA/IOB, targets, meal announcements, CR, and temporary basal behavior.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: A complete sequence of all SMBs, corrections, temporary basals, meals, and resulting IOB is unavailable.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF interacting with UAM/SMB is a more plausible contributor to post-high lows than a weak static ISF. Max basal and max IOB are permissive relative to routine delivery, but neither ceiling was shown to be reached or to cause the observed lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic sensitivity is enabled at 70%, Autosens is disabled, and representative variable sensitivity reached 27.8 mg/dL/U compared with the profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U. Max basal is 12 U/h and max IOB is 25 U, while representative suggestions were constrained below the basal ceiling and representative IOB peaked at 5.935 U.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, ISF, DIA, targets, and safety limits should not be changed together. Limit assessment depends on complete IOB and delivery trajectories.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: There is no isolated comparison of static and dynamic sensitivity and no evidence that either configured safety ceiling became active.

analysis_steps.findings: No numeric prebolus or immediate bolus percentage can be derived. Daytime rises may represent unannounced meals, timing, CR, absorption, or delivery effects, while later hypoglycemia makes a more aggressive meal strategy unsupported.
analysis_steps.evidence: The declared meal_strategies array is empty, there are zero recorded carbohydrate entries, and representative treatments contain no meal treatments. Daytime TAR reached 20.2-32.1%, while UAM/SMB responded with COB zero and some episodes accumulated substantial IOB.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Meal strategy depends on CR, ISF, DIA, targets, SMB/UAM, starting glucose, IOB, meal amount, timing, and absorption.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Numeric prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, meal amount, and meal-linked execution data are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: Regular carbs and e-carbs cannot be compared because neither was recorded. Prolonged highs cannot be attributed to delayed absorption rather than bolus timing, unannounced intake, corrections, or pump delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Carb entries, total recorded carbs, and e-carb entries were all zero; average e-carb duration was null. The August 19 occlusion and pump error provide a non-absorption explanation for at least one episode.
analysis_steps.dependencies: E-carb assessment requires meal-linked separation of meal amount, IOB, SMB/UAM, temporary targets, correction insulin, and pump delivery. E-carbs are not pump extended boluses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb amount, start offset, duration, or meal-linked glucose response is present.

analysis_steps.findings: The evidence supports addressing the overnight safety margin before altering insulin strength. The primary candidate is changing the 00:00 target from 90 to 100 mg/dL while keeping basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and AAPS automation unchanged. Subsequent automation or meal changes require observations collected after this single change.
analysis_steps.evidence: The midnight-to-03:00 period has repeated TBR of approximately 10-18.5%, while daytime highs are confounded by absent meal data and reactive automation. Dynamic ISF and substantial IOB offer competing explanations for post-high lows, so changing insulin-delivery parameters concurrently would prevent attribution.
analysis_steps.dependencies: The target candidate should be evaluated alone. Automation review follows only after overnight glucose and preceding IOB are reassessed; meal strategy follows after meal-linked data collection.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The main unresolved need is a complete timeline linking a recurring meal and overnight period to carbohydrate amount, bolus timing, corrections, SMB/UAM, temporary basal, target, and IOB.

strengths: CGM coverage was 98.7% with no invalid or duplicate entries.
Overall time in range was 86.0% and average glucose was 121.6 mg/dL.
The authoritative profile and all six AAPS decision groups are complete.
The loop frequently recognized predicted low risk and reduced or suspended basal delivery.
No unsupported CR, ISF, DIA, meal, or e-carb value is inferred from the missing meal-linked data.
issues: Time below range was 5.1%, with repeated glucose readings near 41-42 mg/dL.
Late-evening and early-night low exposure was recurrent, including 10.1-18.5% local hourly TBR from 23:00 through 03:00.
Daytime highs were sometimes followed by substantial automated insulin, high IOB, and later hypoglycemia.
Dynamic ISF sometimes produced effective sensitivity substantially stronger than the static 56 mg/dL/U ISF.
No recorded carbohydrates or numeric declared meal strategy are available to distinguish CR, prebolus, absorption, and UAM effects.
The 12 U/h max basal and 25 U max IOB settings are permissive safety ceilings, although neither was demonstrated to be the active cause of an event.

recommendations.title: Review a higher midnight target first
recommendations.description: The strongest repeatable profile-linked signal is recurrent low exposure after midnight. A candidate change from 90 to 100 mg/dL at 00:00 adds safety margin without simultaneously changing insulin strength.

suggested_change.hold_constant: Basal, CR, ISF, DIA, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, and safety limits

recommendations.title: Reassess automation only after the target observation
recommendations.description: Dynamic ISF, UAM/SMB, corrections, and temporary basal are plausible contributors to post-high IOB, but no single automation parameter is isolated. Preserve current automation values while collecting complete insulin and IOB timelines around lows.

suggested_change.action: No automation value change in the same observation period
suggested_change.next_review: Compare post-high lows with Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, correction insulin, temporary basal, target, and IOB

recommendations.title: Collect one recurring meal pattern before meal changes
recommendations.description: Meal-linked data are required before selecting prebolus timing, an immediate bolus percentage, a CR change, or e-carb parameters.

suggested_change.action: Record carbohydrate amount and time, actual prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, starting glucose, IOB, and six-hour SMB/UAM response

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Use 100 mg/dL as the candidate 00:00 target instead of 90 mg/dL, with all dependent profile and AAPS settings held constant during validation.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Local TBR was 11.4% at 00:00, 18.5% at 01:00, and approximately 10% at 02:00-03:00. Residual correction and automation IOB remain important uncertainty, so a modest target change is better supported than altering basal, CR, ISF, DIA, SMB/UAM, or Dynamic ISF.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Compare local 00:00-04:00 TBR, minimum glucose, and insulin delivered or remaining as IOB during the preceding six hours across comparable nights after this change alone.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence shows overnight lows, but uncertainty from preceding corrections, SMB/UAM, targets, and IOB prevents assigning them to basal. This decision depends on evaluating the 00:00 target change first.
Evidence shows only a mild low tendency around 05:00-06:00. Uncertainty from overnight IOB remains, and assessment depends on a fasting-like observation after the target review.
Evidence does not show recurrent low exposure at 08:00 and the later rise may be meal-related. Missing meal context creates uncertainty, so this decision depends on fasting or meal-linked data.
Evidence shows daytime hyperglycemia, but absent carbohydrate data and active UAM/SMB make a basal deficit uncertain. This decision depends on meal-linked or fasting observations.

Evidence shows a 16:00 high period followed by declining glucose and later lows. Uncertainty about meals, corrections, Dynamic ISF, and IOB makes more basal unsafe to infer; reassessment depends on complete post-high timelines.
Evidence shows elevated low exposure around 18:00-19:00, but preceding automated and correction insulin is a strong competing cause. This decision depends on isolating basal from prior IOB.
Evidence includes 15.3% TBR at 19:00, but uncertainty from treatment of earlier highs prevents attributing this to the basal segment. Review depends on a complete preceding insulin timeline.
There is no meal-linked evidence for this CR. Uncertainty is high because carbohydrate amount and bolus execution are absent, and evaluation depends on recorded meals.
Morning rises are observed, but no carbohydrate amount, prebolus, or immediate percentage is available. The uncertainty depends on separating meal timing, UAM/SMB, and basal effects.
Evidence shows daytime highs but no meal-linked dosing information. Uncertainty from unannounced meals, timing, Dynamic ISF, and UAM means any CR change depends on recurring meal observations.
Afternoon highs are followed by evening lows, which argues against strengthening this CR without meal evidence. Uncertainty from IOB and automation requires meal-linked six-hour data first.

Late glucose patterns include substantial low exposure and residual IOB. No meal-linked evidence supports changing this CR, and review depends on separating evening meals from corrections and automation.

Representative effective sensitivity varied widely under Dynamic ISF, so correction outcomes do not isolate the static ISF. Uncertainty from SMB/UAM, temporary basal, food, activity, and IOB means this decision depends on isolated correction evidence.

Evidence shows recurrent local TBR of approximately 10-18.5% from 00:00 through 03:00. Residual IOB remains uncertain, but hypoglycemia risk supports a modest safety-margin candidate; evaluation depends on holding basal and automation constant.
Daytime highs are observed, but meals and automation are unresolved and recurrent lows constrain a lower target. This decision depends on meal-linked evidence rather than hourly glucose alone.

Evidence shows 10.1% TBR at 23:00, but changing both adjacent target segments together would obscure attribution. Uncertainty from evening IOB remains, so this decision depends on first observing the isolated 00:00 target change.

Evidence shows glucose effects through four to six hours but provides no observations beyond six hours that can validate the full DIA. Uncertainty from overlapping insulin and meals means review depends on complete IOB-response data.

Evidence shows UAM/SMB responding to rises with COB zero and substantial IOB in some episodes, but causality is uncertain because Dynamic ISF, corrections, and temporary basal overlap. This decision depends on evaluating the target change and complete insulin timelines first.

The activation settings are internally coherent and no individual condition is isolated as causal. Uncertainty from absent meal announcements and overlapping automation means any change depends on meal-linked and post-high reconstruction.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence suggests possible insulin accumulation, but the configured interval and SMB limits are not independently linked to an event. Uncertainty from Dynamic ISF and other insulin requires assessment after the target change with full SMB and IOB timelines.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: The limits are permissive relative to profile basal and observed IOB, but evidence does not show either ceiling being reached or causing a low. Exact safer replacements are unsupported; review depends on complete delivery and IOB trajectories.

Evidence shows Dynamic ISF sometimes produced much stronger effective sensitivity than the static ISF, making it a plausible contributor to post-high lows. Its independent effect remains uncertain because SMB/UAM and corrections overlap; reassessment depends on first testing the target change alone.
There are no regular carb or e-carb entries with which to test these values. Uncertainty is therefore high, and any change depends on meal-linked carbohydrate and six-hour response data.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Do not assign numeric prebolus minutes or an immediate bolus percentage from this dataset. Record the actual values for a recurring meal, keep SMB/UAM unchanged during observation, and reserve e-carbs for a demonstrated repeatable delayed rise rather than treating them as an extended bolus.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: No meal strategy was numerically declared and no carbohydrate treatments were observed. Daytime rises triggered reactive UAM/SMB with COB zero, while substantial IOB and later lows make a more aggressive meal strategy unsafe to infer. CR, ISF, DIA, targets, and automation all remain dependencies.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For one recurring meal on comparable days, record carbohydrate amount and timestamp, actual prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage, starting glucose, IOB, temporary target and correction use, and SMB/UAM delivery with glucose follow-up through six hours.

exceptions.pattern: Meal-like rise occurring with substantial IOB or after recent correction insulin
exceptions.suggestion: Analyze these episodes separately rather than using them to derive a standard prebolus, immediate percentage, or e-carb pattern.
exceptions.rationale: Recurring high-to-low transitions indicate that residual correction and automation insulin can materially alter the later glucose response.

implementation_steps: Independently confirm the authoritative profile values, time zone, insulin concentration handling, CGM accuracy, and recent pump or site events before interpreting a change.
Discuss and independently verify the single candidate change of the 00:00 target from 90 to 100 mg/dL.
If applied, hold basal, CR, ISF, DIA, 23:00 target, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, and safety limits unchanged during the initial observation.
Monitor glucose closely and compare 00:00-04:00 TBR, minimum glucose, preceding six-hour insulin delivery, and IOB across comparable nights.
Only after the target observation, reconstruct representative post-high lows using corrections, SMB/UAM, temporary basal, Dynamic ISF, target, and IOB before considering one automation change.
Collect a recurring meal dataset before reviewing CR, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, carb absorption, or e-carbs.
Make any later change one at a time and repeat the same observation before proceeding.
education: A favorable average glucose and high time in range can coexist with excessive hypoglycemia; recurrent lows take priority over reducing moderate highs.
Hourly glucose alone is not a basal test when meals, corrections, SMB/UAM, temporary targets, and activity may be present.
Dynamic ISF can make the effective correction sensitivity different from the static profile ISF.
UAM estimates unannounced glucose impact and is not automatic duplicate COB counting.
The configured SMB interval is not the remaining time displayed in an SMB waiting message.
E-carbs model delayed carbohydrate absorption and are not pump extended boluses.
A safety ceiling that was not reached cannot be identified as the cause of an event solely because its configured value is permissive.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not provide medical advice.
Every proposed change must be independently verified, discussed with the appropriate care team when needed, made one at a time, and followed with close glucose monitoring.
No AAPS or profile setting should be changed automatically from this analysis.
Repeated or severe low glucose requires prompt use of the user's established hypoglycemia safety plan and appropriate clinical support.
CGM readings that do not match symptoms or occur near sensor changes should be confirmed according to the user's established device and clinical guidance.
